# omada_radius_profile (Resource)

Manages a RADIUS profile: the servers that 802.1X, MAC authentication and WPA-Enterprise SSIDs authenticate against. `omada_dot1x` is not usable without one.

~> **`shared_secret` is write-only.** The controller returns RADIUS secrets in **plaintext**, which is exactly why this provider never reads them back into state — the same rule the WiFi `psk` follows. A secret you do not re-supply is preserved on update rather than blanked, and it cannot round-trip through `terraform import`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# RADIUS servers for 802.1X / MAC auth / WPA-Enterprise.
#
# shared_secret is a Terraform write-only attribute: it is sent on apply and
# never persisted to state or plan. Source it from a secret store; do not
# hard-code it.
resource "omada_radius_profile" "corp" {
  name = "corp-radius"

  # Mitigates the BlastRADIUS class of attack. Enable unless a legacy client
  # cannot cope.
  require_message_authenticator = true

  auth_server {
    ip            = "10.10.99.5"
    port          = 1812
    shared_secret = var.radius_secret # write-only
  }

  # A second server is used when the first does not answer.
  auth_server {
    ip            = "10.10.99.6"
    shared_secret = var.radius_secret
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Profile name.

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `accounting_enable` (Boolean) Enable RADIUS accounting.
- `auth_server` (Block List) Authentication servers, in priority order. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--auth_server))
- `coa_enable` (Boolean) Accept RADIUS Change-of-Authorization messages.
- `domain_enable` (Boolean) Use a domain name rather than an address for the server.
- `interim_update_enable` (Boolean) Send interim accounting updates.
- `proxy` (Boolean) Act as a RADIUS proxy.
- `require_message_authenticator` (Boolean) Require the Message-Authenticator attribute. Recommended: it mitigates the BlastRADIUS class of attack.
- `site` (String) Site name. Defaults to the primary site. Changing forces replacement.
- `tunnel_reply_enable` (Boolean) Honour tunnel attributes in the RADIUS reply.
- `wireless_vlan_assignment` (Boolean) Let RADIUS assign the wireless client's VLAN.

### Read-Only

- `built_in_server` (Boolean) Whether this is the controller's built-in RADIUS server. Read-only.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `site_id` (String)

<a id="nestedblock--auth_server"></a>
### Nested Schema for `auth_server`

Required:

- `ip` (String) Server address.

Optional:

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `port` (Number) Authentication port. Defaults to `1812`.
- `radsec_enable` (Boolean) Wrap RADIUS in TLS (RadSec).
- `shared_secret` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Shared secret. **Write-only**: supplied on apply and never persisted to state or plan. Omit it on a later apply to keep the secret already configured on the controller.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# By profile ID, or "<site>/<id>".
# Shared secrets cannot be imported — the provider never reads them back — so
# re-supply them in configuration after importing.
terraform import omada_radius_profile.corp 6a64ca02bb62a10bd62c4233
```
